text: Sergio Flamigni (22 October 1925 – 10 December 2025) was an Italian politician and writer affiliated with the Italian Communist Party (PCI). He participated in several parliamentary investigative commissions focusing on the murder of Aldo Moro, the Propaganda Due scandal, and the Italian Mafia. Born in Forlì on 22 October 1925, Flamigni began his political engagement in 1941 as a member of a clandestine group of young anti-fascists in his hometown and later joined the Communist Party of Italy. In 1943, he was appointed secretary of the communist youth movement in Forlì and became part of the party's clandestine committee in the city. He actively fought as a partisan during the Italian resistance movement against the German occupation. In 1952, he was named secretary of CGIL, the left-wing main trade union in Forlì, and later served as secretary of the local PCI section. In 1959, he was elected to the party's national central committee, and the following year became regional coordinator for Emilia-Romagna. He served on the city council of Forlì from 1956 to 1960 and on the provincial council from 1960 to 1964. Flamigni was elected to the Italian Chamber of Deputies in 1968 and remained a member until 1979, when he became an Italian Senator. During his time in Parliament, he worked on commissions investigating the Mafia, the kidnapping of Aldo Moro, and the Propaganda Due secret lodge, and he authored books on these subjects. He passed away on 10 December 2025, at the age of 100.
